claims.text: A hybrid CE-ML-thermodynamic-integration framework will predict refractory-HEA melting temperatures and entropies of fusion with less than 5% error relative to experiment.
The proposed framework will outperform standard CALPHAD extrapolations at extreme temperatures.
NbMoTaW and W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can be treated as disordered bcc solid solutions at 0 K.
Efficient computational tools are needed to screen the vast compositional space of HEAs.
Cluster expansion captures the energetic landscape of local atomic configurations and permits efficient sampling of configurational space.
A GPR or neural-network potential trained on sparse DFT energies and forces can accurately represent multiple SRO states and the high-energy liquid state.
MD thermodynamic integration with the ML potential can determine solid-liquid coexistence or solid-liquid free-energy differences while including anharmonic vibrational effects.
Refractory HEAs such as NbMoTaW typically melt above 2000 K.
The target composition space contains five to seven principal elements.
SRO clusters and severe local lattice distortions are characteristic of refractory HEAs and significantly alter their vibrational density of states and melting free-energy barrier.
Standard CALPHAD calculations depend on databases assembled from lower-order alloy descriptions.
CALPHAD extrapolations fail to capture nonlinear multicomponent interactions and strong local chemical ordering in HEAs.
Harmonic approximations often overestimate the configurational entropy of the liquid phase.
The ML potential supplies liquid-state accuracy at substantially lower cost than ab initio MD over the entire phase space.
Entropy of fusion increases with compositional complexity because of enhanced vibrational anharmonicity.
Standard CALPHAD will deviate from experimental melting temperatures by more than 15% and fail to reproduce their nonlinear composition dependence.
The method is valid for substitutional RHEA solid solutions with disordered liquids but may fail when intermetallic formation dominates or liquid SRO is absent from the ML training set.
Prediction accuracy depends strongly on including representative high-temperature liquid configurations and relevant SRO motifs in the DFT training set.
A classical potential trained mainly on 0 K or 300 K DFT data may incur errors in the strongly anharmonic regime above 2000 K.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires an error strictly below 5%, but the falsification rule triggers only when error exceeds 5%; an error exactly equal to 5% satisfies neither criterion.
The experimental design initially specifies selection of one composition, whereas falsification of the entropy-of-fusion trend requires results for at least two distinct compositions.
